html:
SMTO-GWT-0022 — SMTO couldn't confirm a secure connection to the Gateway

GUID: 4202ee03-640e-4980-8b9b-cda3b2c01c12
Slug: gateway-tls-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO checks the Gateway's security certificate before sending it any work. That check failed, so SMTO stopped before sending anything and no command ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand this Gateway and select Edit. Make sure Host and Port are the address of the Gateway, not another program. If the address points to a different program, it can't complete the Gateway's secure greeting.
  2. Check that the date and time are correct and set automatically on both the SMTO server computer and the Gateway computer. A security certificate counts as valid only between two dates, so a wrong clock makes a good certificate look expired.
  3. Select Check connection for this Gateway. This repeats the security check; nothing was sent to the Gateway before, so it is safe to check again.
  4. If the Gateway was recently reinstalled, ask the person who manages it to confirm it is the same machine before anyone selects Forget trusted identity. Forgetting the saved identity makes SMTO trust whatever answers at that address next.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected with the Secure badge in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't turn off security checks or switch the Gateway to an insecure connection to get past this message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Pinned TLS setup to the Gateway failed: the handshake failed, the peer certificate was outside its validity period or used an unsupported key or signature, the record changed during enrollment, or the trust record could not be saved.

What this means

  • Secure transport setup failed its handshake, certificate validity, key or signature requirements, pinned-identity verification, current enrollment checks or trust persistence. The code uses explicit public-key verification, so a CA-chain problem is not established by this category. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Secure transport setup failed its handshake, certificate validity, key or signature requirements, pinned-identity verification, current enrollment checks or trust persistence. The code uses explicit public-key verification, so a CA-chain problem is not established by this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained TLS or trust-persistence reason, certificate dates, supported key, saved pin and current enrollment; check clocks when validity dates fail.

How to fix it

  • Read the Technical details for the specific failure (handshake failed, certificate validity, unsupported identity key or signature, trust could not be persisted). Check that the profile's host and port point to the Gateway's HTTPS listener, that both hosts' clocks are correct (the certificate's notBefore/notAfter is checked), and that the Gateway certificate is a 2048-bit-or-larger RSA self-signed certificate with a SHA-256/384/512 signature; then use Check connection. Never disable verification, and use Forget trusted identity only after confirming the machine.
  • Repair the specific certificate, identity, clock, enrollment or storage failure shown by the retained evidence. Preserve pin verification and verify the machine before deliberate re-enrollment.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway completes secure identity verification and persists the matching trust record before application work.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically trust a replacement identity or disable certificate verification.
